Termux:API provides commands to access Android features from the terminal. Common commands:

•termux-battery-status •battery info
•termux-camera-photo •take a photo
•termux-clipboard-get / termux-clipboard-set •clipboard
•termux-notification •post a notification
•termux-toast •show a toast
•termux-vibrate •vibrate device
•termux-location •get GPS location
•termux-sms-list / termux-sms-send •SMS
•termux-tts-speak •text to speech
•termux-wifi-connectioninfo •WiFi info

Install the termux-api package first:
pkg install termux-api

Termux:Boot runs scripts automatically when the device starts.

To add a boot script:

1. Create the directory:
 mkdir -p ~/.termux/boot
2. Place executable scripts in ~/.termux/boot/
3. Scripts run in sorted order on boot.

Example (~/.termux/boot/start-ssh):
 #!/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/sh
 termux-wake-lock
 sshd

High Risk Command - Virtual Machine Environment

This command is being executed inside a virtual machine environment and may cause irreversible damage to the virtual machine system, including but not limited to: virtual machine data loss, virtual machine system corruption, inability to start the virtual machine, etc. Please carefully evaluate the necessity and safety of this command before execution.

This command is being executed on a remote system connected via SSH, which may cause irreversible damage to the remote system, including but not limited to: remote data loss, remote system corruption, service interruption, etc. If the remote system is a production environment, executing this command may result in service interruption, data loss, or even legal liability. Please carefully evaluate the necessity and safety of this command before execution.

This disk-level command will run on a remote system connected via SSH. Operations such as dd, mkfs, fdisk and parted may overwrite raw disks, destroy partition tables and erase all data permanently. Mis-specifying a device path can brick the whole remote host, and damaged data is almost unrecoverable. If the remote system is a production environment, executing this command may result in service interruption, massive data loss, or even legal liability. Please double-check target device path and evaluate necessity before execution.

This disk-level command will run on a remote Windows system connected via SSH. Operations such as format, diskpart, and bcdedit can format partitions, wipe disk partition tables, modify or delete system boot configurations. diskpart\'s clean / clean all commands will erase all partition information on the disk, and clean-all will overwrite all sectors on the disk, making data almost unrecoverable. Specifying a wrong disk number or drive letter can cause data loss on the entire disk; even while the system is running, administrator privileges can destroy data on non-system volumes. If the remote system is a production environment, executing this command will cause massive data loss, business interruption, and even prevent the system from booting, with potential legal consequences. Please carefully verify disk numbers and drive letters before execution.

You are about to shut down or restart a remote system connected via SSH.

After you confirm, the remote host will terminate all running programs and services and the SSH session will be disconnected. If you choose to shut down, and there is no one physically present at the remote device or the device does not have Wake-on-LAN capability, the system will remain offline and you will not be able to restore it remotely.

If this is a production environment, this operation will cause service interruption and potential business losses.
